content.comment_body: Hello all, I'm developing a custom web page using [product_name] Web Editor for my application inside a [product_name] Basis Module ([article_no]). I want a way for my PLC application to trigger a message text that appears directly on the web page. Ideally, I'd like to show the message text block from [product_name] without needing to access the physical display. The original [company_name] web page displays the message in its standard web display, so my configuration seems correct, but I haven't found how to do this with my customized web page. Is this achievable, and if so, how?

Could you clarify which web server you are referring to? The [product_name] module offers two web servers: a basic web editor and an advanced web server. Using the simple web server, you can display message texts, but with the advanced one you cannot.

Hi, I assume 'simple web server' means the standard [company_name] offering, while 'advanced' refers to custom sites built using [product_name] Web Editor. If that's correct, then I'm working with the advanced server.

[product_name] Web Editor is just a platform to build user-defined web pages, which are shown in browsers via the extended web server. The editor itself cannot display content and lacks a simulation mode like [product_name] Soft Comfort. At the moment, there is no function within [product_name] Web Editor to link a message text directly from the [product_name] module. Perhaps you could implement something custom if you are familiar with HTML5.
Thanks for your clarification. So it seems I cannot link the message text in the advanced web server. I'll follow your suggestion and attempt a custom solution using HTML5. Thank you.

Hi, here's a workaround: Make a screenshot of the desired message text as shown on the [product_name] display. Then, within [product_name] Web Editor, connect the signal that triggers the message to display this screenshot instead. Hope this is useful.

Another option: Set up a flag in [product_name] Soft Comfort that follows after the block for message text. In [product_name] Web Editor, you can then display a digital value with state-dependent text based on that flag's logic.

Alternatively, use a digital network output instead of a flag. Nevertheless, this isn't quite the solution the user wants. Direct message text from [product_name] can only be displayed on the [product_name] display or certain panels, or through the basic/simple web server—not the extended one.

In [product_name] Web Editor, it's actually better because you can show digital values as either text or graphical images. Also, you can set longer words or more characters than what's allowed on the [product_name] display. So there's little reason to stick to only the display text. [product_name] Web Editor offers more flexibility.
Why the user wants this is their choice.
It's even better that the latest [product_name] Web Editor version can resize text when the newest software is available.
It seems the user hasn’t tried building their own custom site with [product_name] Web Editor.
I'm waiting for the new [product_name] module and updated software. [company_name] did a lot of marketing with the first extended web server, but it was not as impressive as claimed.
I've seen some examples of the newest [product_name] Web Editor, and currently it shouldn't be an issue.
I'll still wait and see. Promotional videos tend to exaggerate features and present products better than reality.

analysis.insight_summary: Users want to dynamically display PLC application message texts on custom web pages created with [product_name] Web Editor for a [product_name] Basis Module. The main issue is that the extended web server doesn't allow direct integration or display of message text blocks from the module, as the simple web server or hardware display does. Suggested workarounds like screenshots or using digital value indicators do not deliver true dynamic updates or full integration, which limits the user's goals.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to show dynamic message text blocks from the [product_name] module on a custom web page built via [product_name] Web Editor, updating in real time, without depending on the hardware display.
